data_provenance: Research dataset: era A (Drought Atlas of India SPEI reconstruction, 1901-2025), era B (CHIRPS v2.0, ERA5-Land and MODIS MOD13A3 gridded product, 1981-01 to 2026-09) and era C (bias-corrected CMIP6, 2015-2100), aggregated to 724 Indian districts. Missing values are never imputed.
spatial_units: administrative districts (36 states/union territories, 724 units as supplied)
spatial_resolution: district-level aggregation (simplified boundary geometry served for visualisation)
area_method: Precomputed equal-area statistics (Lambert Azimuthal Equal-Area centred at 22.5N, 79.5E). Areas are never derived from degree-coordinate arithmetic.
reference_period: SPI/SPEI and SMA climatology 1981-2020; VCI 2000-present (per-calendar-month fitting; see methodology)

aggregation.areal_mean: area-weighted mean over constituent districts using precomputed equal-area district areas
aggregation.affected_area: sum of equal-area district areas whose indicator value falls in a drought class
aggregation.completeness: valid district-month observations divided by expected district-month observations

events.severity: cumulative deficit below the -1.0 truncation level summed over event months

indicators.label: SPI-1
indicators.name: Standardized Precipitation Index, 1-month
indicators.tooltip: One-month standardized precipitation anomaly: short-term meteorological moisture status.
indicators.description: SPI-1 standardizes current-month precipitation against its per-calendar-month climatological distribution, isolating month-to-month meteorological fluctuations.
indicators.classification: SPI/SPEI convention (McKee et al., 1993; Vicente-Serrano et al., 2010)

indicators.label: SPI-3
indicators.name: Standardized Precipitation Index, 3-month
indicators.tooltip: Three-month standardized precipitation anomaly: seasonal (roughly a monsoon-season) drought signal.
indicators.description: SPI-3 aggregates precipitation over the preceding three months and standardizes it per calendar month; it is a common operational window for seasonal agricultural drought.
indicators.classification: SPI/SPEI convention (McKee et al., 1993; Vicente-Serrano et al., 2010)
indicators.availability_note: Source record begins 1981-03; 2 month(s) before this are not available.

indicators.label: SPI-6
indicators.name: Standardized Precipitation Index, 6-month
indicators.tooltip: Six-month standardized precipitation anomaly: medium-term hydrological drought signal.
indicators.description: SPI-6 reflects precipitation accumulated over half a year and correlates with reservoir storage and streamflow anomalies in many Indian basins.
indicators.classification: SPI/SPEI convention (McKee et al., 1993; Vicente-Serrano et al., 2010)
indicators.availability_note: Source record begins 1981-06; 5 month(s) before this are not available.

indicators.label: SPI-12
indicators.name: Standardized Precipitation Index, 12-month
indicators.tooltip: Twelve-month standardized precipitation anomaly: inter-annual drought signal.
indicators.description: SPI-12 aggregates a full water year and is used for long-term water-resource and groundwater drought assessment.
indicators.classification: SPI/SPEI convention (McKee et al., 1993; Vicente-Serrano et al., 2010)
indicators.availability_note: Source record begins 1981-12; 11 month(s) before this are not available.

indicators.label: SPEI-1
indicators.name: Standardized Precipitation Evapotranspiration Index, 1-month
indicators.tooltip: One-month standardized climatic water balance (precipitation minus potential evapotranspiration).
indicators.description: SPEI-1 standardizes the monthly climatic water balance, adding the effect of atmospheric evaporative demand to the SPI-1 signal.
indicators.classification: SPI/SPEI convention (McKee et al., 1993; Vicente-Serrano et al., 2010)

indicators.label: SPEI-3
indicators.name: Standardized Precipitation Evapotranspiration Index, 3-month
indicators.tooltip: Three-month standardized climatic water balance: temperature-sensitive seasonal drought signal.
indicators.description: SPEI-3 is the seasonal water-balance analogue of SPI-3; differences between the two isolate the evaporative-demand contribution to drought.
indicators.classification: SPI/SPEI convention (McKee et al., 1993; Vicente-Serrano et al., 2010)
indicators.availability_note: Source record begins 1981-03; 2 month(s) before this are not available.

indicators.label: SPEI-6
indicators.name: Standardized Precipitation Evapotranspiration Index, 6-month
indicators.tooltip: Six-month standardized climatic water balance: medium-term drought including demand trends.
indicators.description: SPEI-6 is the medium-term water-balance drought signal; because it includes potential evapotranspiration it responds to warming trends that SPI cannot see.
indicators.classification: SPI/SPEI convention (McKee et al., 1993; Vicente-Serrano et al., 2010)
indicators.availability_note: Source record begins 1981-06; 5 month(s) before this are not available.

indicators.label: SPEI-12
indicators.name: Standardized Precipitation Evapotranspiration Index, 12-month
indicators.tooltip: Twelve-month standardized climatic water balance: inter-annual drought including demand trends.
indicators.description: SPEI-12 is the annual water-balance drought indicator used for multi-year drought characterization.
indicators.classification: SPI/SPEI convention (McKee et al., 1993; Vicente-Serrano et al., 2010)
indicators.availability_note: Source record begins 1981-12; 11 month(s) before this are not available.

indicators.label: Soil Moisture Anomaly
indicators.name: Soil Moisture Anomaly (SMA)
indicators.tooltip: Percent anomaly of root-zone-equivalent soil moisture versus its seasonal climatology.
indicators.description: SMA expresses soil-moisture departure from the per-calendar-month climatological mean as a percentage anomaly; negative values indicate soil-water deficit. Classification thresholds are indicator-specific (see methodology).

indicators.label: Vegetation Condition Index
indicators.name: Vegetation Condition Index (VCI)
indicators.tooltip: Percentage vegetation condition between historical stress and optimum (Kogan-style scaling).
indicators.description: VCI rescales a vegetation index between its historical minimum (stress) and maximum (optimum); low values indicate vegetation under drought stress. Thresholds follow the Kogan (1995)-style convention and are documented in the methodology.
indicators.availability_note: Source record begins 2000-02; 229 month(s) before this are not available.

sources.name: CHIRPS daily precipitation v2.0 Final (Funk et al., 2015) via Google Earth Engine
sources.role: rainfall input for SPI and SPEI
sources.description: Climate Hazards Center Infrared Precipitation with Stations, daily 0.05 degree, 1981-present, accessed through the Earth Engine catalog asset UCSB-CHG/CHIRPS/DAILY. GEE currently distributes the v2.0 Final product; the local download route uses v3.0. Public domain.

sources.name: ERA5-Land monthly aggregates (Munoz-Sabater et al., 2021) via Google Earth Engine
sources.description: ECMWF ERA5-Land monthly aggregated reanalysis, 0.1 degree, 1950-present, Earth Engine asset ECMWF/ERA5_LAND/MONTHLY_AGGR. Potential evaporation is the monthly accumulated depth; soil moisture is the mean of volumetric layers 1-3 (0-100 cm). Copernicus licence (attribution).

sources.name: MODIS/Terra MOD13A3 v061 monthly NDVI (Didan, 2015) via Google Earth Engine
sources.role: NDVI input for the Vegetation Condition Index
sources.description: MODIS Terra monthly vegetation indices at 1 km, 2000-present, Earth Engine asset MODIS/061/MOD13A3, NDVI scaled by 0.0001. NASA LP DAAC open data.

sources.name: India administrative boundaries (districts, 2011-census demarcation)
sources.description: Community-maintained district GeoJSON, generalised for web use; 724 districts, 36 states/UTs. Not authoritative for legal boundary determination.

citation: Deshmukh, A. (2026). Drought Intelligence Explorer: a multi-era district drought record and analytics platform for India (Version 2.0.0) [computer software]. Zenodo. https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.24444860 · data snapshot v2026.09, archived at https://data.ankitdeshmukh.com/v2026.09/ · concept DOI (latest version): https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.24113363 · archived v1.0.0 release: https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.24113364

doi.v2_0_0_note: version DOI for v2.0.0, minted 2026-11-22 by the GitHub-Zenodo integration; the concept DOI 10.5281/zenodo.24113363 always resolves to the latest version

disclaimer: Research build: values are derived from the cited public datasets and gridded sources, aggregated to administrative districts. They are model/reanalysis-based estimates, not official drought declarations, and must not be used as the sole basis for operational decisions.

era_c.label: Projections 2015-2100
era_c.banner: PROJECTIONS (era C) - QDM-bias-corrected CMIP6, SSP2-4.5 / SSP5-8.5, IMD-calibrated (reference 1981-2020). Simulations, never forecasts; never spliced with observed data; presented with ensemble spread and agreement (X2/X3), never the median alone.

ensemble.criterion_rule: core = largest inter-rank composite gap; extend to size_range[0] by reweighting-stability order (Dirichlet weight perturbations); cap at size_range[1] and candidate count (see config/validation.yaml ranking.subset_criterion)

pet.seam: per-era PET (decision E): era B ERA5-Land PET frozen; era C Hargreaves applied identically to reference and model temperature

honesty: spread + agreement shown alongside the median (X2/X3)

source.title: CMIP6 historical and SSP simulations, bias-corrected
source.models: 22-model archive; 8-model committed subset recorded in era_c.ensemble
source.reference_dataset: IMD 0.25-degree gridded rainfall (Pai et al., 2014) and temperature (Srivastava et al., 2009)
methods: Hargreaves-Samani PET (1985) applied identically to reference and model temperature
gamma SPI / log-logistic SPEI on the 0.25-degree grid, aggregated to the 724-district fabric

source.licence: CMIP6 model output is subject to each model's terms of use (see the ESGF record); IMD reference data per IMD terms. Derived DIE products are redistributed with attribution; the application code is MIT.

dir_agreement.definition: fraction of subset models whose effective-window mean is drier (lower z) than their own 1981-2014 base mean; window-constant per district; a count of models, never a probability
dir_agreement.window_note: overlap of the configured window 2081-2100 with the record 2015-2100

era_a.label: Atlas reconstruction (SPEI) 1901-2025
era_a.banner: ERA A (reconstruction) - Drought Atlas of India SPEI at 1/4/12-month scales, 0.05-degree grid area-weighted onto the 724-district fabric (route OD4). A reconstruction, never spliced with the era-B Gridded Multi-Source Product or era-C projections (R2); era-labelled on every surface.

source.title: Drought Atlas of India, 1901-2025
source.citation: Chuphal, D. S., Kushwaha, A. P., Aadhar, S., & Mishra, V. (2024). Drought Atlas of India, 1901-2025 (Version 2) [Data set]. Zenodo. https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.20368514

era_a.route: geometric area-weighted aggregation of the 0.05-degree grid onto 724 districts (Sutherland-Hodgman LAEA clip weights, gcm-pipeline/06 machinery); the Atlas's own 742-polygon/732-series fabric is QA-only, never published
era_a.missing: the six island districts have no Atlas grid cells (documented ocean mask); values absent, never imputed (R10)
era_a.seam: era A and era B are NEVER spliced; the 1981-2025 overlap is cross-validation material only (M6.6, register D6 comparison window)

data_host: Cloudflare R2 (public custom domain; Parquet + wide CSVs read over HTTP Range)
